t: For fixing IDV, the percentage depreciation applicable to a vehicle aged more than 3 years but not exceeding 4 years is:
e: The IDV schedule is 5% (up to 6 months), 15% (6 months to 1 year), 20% (1-2 years), 30% (2-3 years), 40% (3-4 years) and 50% (4-5 years).

t: A Personal Accident policy has a capital sum insured of Rs 10 lakh. The insured loses one hand in an accident (permanent partial disablement rated at 50%). The benefit payable is:
e: PPD is paid as the specified percentage of CSI: 50% x Rs 10 lakh = Rs 5 lakh.

t: The Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha policy applies to risks where the total value at risk is:
o: Above Rs 5 crore and up to Rs 50 crore
e: Laghu Udyam Suraksha is the standard product for mid-sized enterprises with value at risk between Rs 5 crore and Rs 50 crore.

t: Which of the following is available only as an add-on cover under the SFSP policy?
e: Terrorism is excluded from SFSP and is granted as an add-on through the Indian Market Terrorism Risk Insurance Pool at pool rates.

t: Which of the following perils is covered under ICC (B) but NOT under ICC (C)?
o: Vessel being stranded, grounded, sunk or capsized
Entry of sea, lake or river water into the vessel or container
e: ICC (C) is the narrowest cover; perils such as earthquake, entry of sea water and washing overboard are covered only from ICC (B) upwards.

t: Under PMFBY, the maximum premium payable by a farmer for Kharif food and oilseed crops is:
e: Farmer share is 2% for Kharif, 1.5% for Rabi and 5% for annual commercial and horticultural crops; the balance actuarial premium is subsidised by Centre and State.

t: General insurance business in India (other than motor third party) was de-tariffed with effect from:
e: IRDA withdrew tariff rates for fire, engineering, motor OD and other classes from 1 January 2007, leaving motor TP under administered pricing.

t: In rating terminology, the 'burning cost' of a risk or portfolio is:
o: Claims incurred divided by the exposure (sum insured) over a period
Total losses divided by partial losses
e: Burning cost expresses actual loss experience as a rate against exposure and is the starting point for experience-based pricing.

t: An 'ex-gratia' payment by an insurer is:
o: A payment legally due under the policy terms
A recovery obtained from the reinsurer
A goodwill payment made without admitting liability under the policy
e: Ex-gratia settlements are discretionary payments made for commercial or compassionate reasons where the claim is not strictly admissible.

t: Under a Liability Only (Act) motor policy, the standard limit for third party property damage is:
e: TP death or bodily injury liability is unlimited, while TPPD is covered up to Rs 7.5 lakh (the insured may restrict it to the statutory Rs 6,000 for a discount).

t: Which section of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 makes third party insurance compulsory for a vehicle used in a public place?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 146 provides that no person shall use a motor vehicle in a public place unless a policy complying with Chapter XI is in force.

t: An excess (deductible) in a policy is:
o: The maximum amount the insurer will pay per claim
The first part of every loss which is borne by the insured
A depreciation deduction applied to replaced parts
A loading on premium for adverse features
e: The excess is deducted from each admissible claim, eliminating small claims and encouraging the insured to take care.

t: An Erection All Risks (EAR) policy is specifically designed to cover:
o: Civil construction works such as buildings and bridges
Erection, installation and testing of plant and machinery
e: EAR covers machinery and equipment from arrival at site through storage, erection, testing and commissioning, while CAR covers civil engineering projects.

t: Under the SFSP policy, impact damage to the insured property caused by a road vehicle belonging to the insured is:
o: Excluded, as impact damage covers only vehicles not belonging to the insured or his employees
Covered up to 10% of the sum insured
e: The impact damage peril covers damage by rail/road vehicles or animals not belonging to or under the control of the insured or any occupier of the premises.

t: GIC Re is best described as:
o: A direct public sector general insurer
e: General Insurance Corporation of India was designated the national reinsurer in 2000 and no longer writes direct business.

t: The Certificate of Insurance for a motor vehicle is a statutory requirement under:
o: Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
e: Section 147 of the MV Act requires that a policy of insurance is effective only when the insurer issues a certificate of insurance in the prescribed form.

t: Under standard health insurance definitions, 'hospitalisation' requires admission in a hospital for a minimum period of:
e: Hospitalisation means in-patient admission for at least 24 consecutive hours, except for specified day-care procedures which need less time due to technological advancement.

t: Under the SFSP policy, which of the following losses is excluded?
o: Impact damage by a third party's road vehicle
Damage by storm, tempest and flood
Loss due to spontaneous combustion of stocks
e: Fire damage arising from fermentation, natural heating or spontaneous combustion is an exclusion under the fire peril and must be bought as an add-on.

t: A 'co-payment' clause in a health policy means:
o: The insurer pays the entire bill and recovers from the hospital
The insured bears a specified percentage of every admissible claim
Two insurers share the claim equally
The premium is paid in instalments
e: Co-pay is a cost-sharing device under which the insured pays a fixed percentage (e.g. 10% or 20%) of each claim, typically for senior citizens or to reduce premium.

t: A health policy has a 20% co-payment on all claims. The admissible hospitalisation expenses are Rs 1,00,000. The insurer pays:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Co-payment is the percentage of each admissible claim borne by the insured; 20% of Rs 1 lakh is borne by the insured, so Rs 80,000 is paid.

t: The No Claim Bonus applicable on own damage premium after three consecutive claim-free years is:
e: NCB slabs are 20%, 25%, 35%, 45% and 50% for one to five consecutive claim-free years respectively.

t: In a motor theft claim, the document that confirms the police have been unable to trace the stolen vehicle is the:
e: The insurer settles a theft claim after obtaining the FIR and the police final (untraced) report, along with RC transfer, keys and a letter of subrogation.

t: An Electronic Equipment Insurance policy is typically divided into sections covering:
o: Equipment, external data media, and increased cost of working
e: EEI has Section I (equipment), Section II (external data media and cost of reinstating data) and Section III (increased cost of working for substitute equipment).

t: Under IRDAI norms, a grievance received by an insurer must be resolved and the complainant informed within:
e: Insurers must acknowledge grievances promptly and resolve them within 14 days (two weeks); unresolved complaints may be escalated to the Insurance Ombudsman.

t: An insurer has a 10-line surplus treaty with a retention of Rs 20 lakh per risk. The maximum amount it can cede to the treaty on a single risk is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Treaty capacity equals the number of lines multiplied by the retention (one line); 10 lines x Rs 20 lakh = Rs 200 lakh of cession.

t: Under a standard Burglary (Business Premises) policy, the insured peril is theft:
o: Of any kind from the premises
Committed by domestic servants or employees
Following actual, forcible and violent entry into or exit from the premises, or hold-up
e: The burglary policy requires visible evidence of forcible and violent entry or exit (or robbery/hold-up); mere theft, pilferage or infidelity of employees is excluded.

t: A Directors' and Officers' (D&O) liability policy covers:
o: Personal liability of directors and officers for wrongful acts committed in their managerial capacity
e: D&O protects individual directors and officers (and reimburses the company where it indemnifies them) against claims alleging breach of duty, negligence or misstatement.

t: Which of the following losses is excluded under a Machinery Breakdown policy?
o: Damage due to faulty workmanship or defective material
e: MB covers sudden unforeseen mechanical and electrical breakdown; fire and allied perils are excluded since they are insurable under the fire policy.

t: Moral hazard in underwriting refers to:
o: The physical condition of the property insured
The attitude, honesty and conduct of the insured
The geographical location of the risk
The class of construction of the building
e: Moral hazard arises from the character and behaviour of the proposer, such as carelessness or dishonesty, and cannot be measured by physical inspection.

t: In cattle insurance, the insured animal is identified by:
o: Hot-iron branding on the hind leg
An ear tag fixed at the time of insurance
Entry in the village panchayat register
e: A numbered ear tag is applied at inception and must be surrendered at the time of claim; the 'no tag, no claim' condition applies.

t: Statements made by the proposer in the proposal form, which is declared to be the basis of the contract, are treated as:
o: Warranties forming the basis of the contract
e: The declaration in the proposal form makes the answers the basis of the contract, so a material misstatement entitles the insurer to avoid the policy.

t: Which of the following is NOT a statutory defence available to the insurer against a third party claim under Section 149(2) of the MV Act, 1988?
o: Vehicle driven by a person not duly licensed
Vehicle used for hire or reward when not permitted
Driver was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident
Policy obtained by non-disclosure of a material fact
e: Drunken driving is not one of the statutory breaches listed in Section 149(2); the listed defences relate to use, driver's licence and misrepresentation.

t: Under IRDAI's standard definitions, a 'pre-existing disease' is one diagnosed or for which treatment was advised within how many months prior to the first policy?
e: PED is any condition diagnosed or treated within 36 months prior to the first policy issued by the insurer, and the PED waiting period cannot exceed 36 months.

t: A consignment is insured under a marine cargo policy at CIF value Rs 10 lakh plus 10%. Goods are totally lost at sea. The insurer pays:
e: Marine cargo policies are valued policies; in a total loss the agreed insured value (CIF + 10% = Rs 11 lakh) is payable irrespective of actual market value.

t: A driver without a valid driving licence causes an accident injuring a pedestrian, who obtains an award from the MACT. The insurer:
o: May repudiate the third-party claim outright
Need not pay as the Tribunal must dismiss such a claim
Must pay the award to the third party and recover the amount from the insured
e: Under the 'pay and recover' principle laid down by the Supreme Court, the insurer satisfies the award to the innocent victim and then recovers from the insured for breach of policy conditions.

t: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act 1938 requires that:
o: Premium is received in advance before the risk is assumed
Every policy carries a free-look clause
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). No risk may be assumed unless the premium has been received in advance or is guaranteed in the manner prescribed.

t: To port a health insurance policy to another insurer, the policyholder must apply to the new insurer at least how many days before the renewal date?
e: Portability guidelines require the request to be made at least 45 days (and not more than 60 days) before expiry so that waiting period credits can be transferred.

t: A Product Liability policy indemnifies the insured against:
o: Legal liability for third-party bodily injury or property damage caused by a defect in the product
Expenses of recalling the product from the market
The cost of repairing or replacing the defective product
A guarantee of the quality or performance of the product
e: Product liability covers compensation and defence costs for injury or damage caused by the product sold; the product itself and recall costs are excluded.

t: A quota share treaty is:
o: A facultative arrangement negotiated risk by risk
An excess of loss cover on a portfolio
A proportional treaty under which a fixed percentage of every risk is ceded
e: In a quota share treaty, premiums and losses on every risk in the class are shared between cedant and reinsurer in a predetermined ratio.

t: In Public Liability (Industrial Risks) policies, the limits of indemnity for any one accident (AOA) and any one year (AOY) are offered in ratios such as:
e: The insured selects an AOA limit and an AOY limit, with the AOY being one to four times the AOA, and the premium rate varies with the ratio chosen.

t: Which specialised insurer in India is primarily engaged in writing crop insurance business?
o: Agriculture Insurance Company of India Ltd
e: AIC of India was set up in 2002 as a specialised insurer for crop and allied rural risks and is the largest implementing agency under PMFBY.

t: Under a Jewellers Block policy, Section I covers:
o: Property entrusted to brokers, agents and cutters
Stock and goods in trade while in the insured's premises against fire, burglary, hold-up, etc.
Stock in transit by registered post or angadia
e: Section I covers stock at the premises; Section II covers stock in custody of the insured and others outside; Section III covers transit; Section IV covers fixtures.

t: Under the reinstatement value clause of a fire policy, reinstatement must normally be commenced and carried out within what period from the date of loss?
e: Reinstatement value basis (replacement new without depreciation) applies only if the work is carried out within 12 months, failing which settlement is on market value.

t: Under the Bharat Griha Raksha policy for home building and contents, the condition of underinsurance (average):
o: Applies exactly as in the SFSP policy
Applies to contents but not to the building
e: Bharat Griha Raksha has a complete waiver of underinsurance; the insurer does not reduce the claim even if the sum insured is less than the value at risk.

t: Nomination and assignment of a life insurance policy are governed respectively by which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 39 deals with nomination; Section 38 with assignment and transfer.

t: Following the Supreme Court direction of 2018, long-term third party insurance at the time of sale of a new vehicle is for:
o: 3 years for private cars and 5 years for two-wheelers
5 years for private cars and 3 years for two-wheelers
3 years for both private cars and two-wheelers
5 years for both private cars and two-wheelers
e: New private cars must carry 3-year TP cover and new two-wheelers 5-year TP cover, so that vehicles do not go uninsured after the first year.

t: A property worth Rs 50 lakh is insured with Insurer A for Rs 20 lakh and Insurer B for Rs 30 lakh on identical terms. A loss of Rs 10 lakh occurs. Under the principle of contribution, Insurer A pays:
e: Rateable contribution is in proportion to sums insured: A pays 10 x 20/50 = Rs 4 lakh and B pays Rs 6 lakh.

t: Under a Householders package policy, jewellery and valuables worn or carried outside the home are covered under the:
e: The all risks section covers jewellery, valuables and specified items anywhere in India, whereas the fire and burglary sections apply only within the premises.

t: Mr Sharma was diagnosed with diabetes one year before taking a health policy with a 36-month PED waiting period. In the second policy year he is hospitalised for diabetic complications. The claim is:
o: Not payable, as the PED waiting period is incomplete
e: Diabetes is a declared pre-existing disease; claims arising from it are payable only after the 36 months of continuous coverage have been completed.

t: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938 provides that:
o: No risk shall be assumed unless premium is received in advance
Policies must be issued within 30 days of proposal
Proposal forms must be countersigned by the agent
Claims must be settled within 30 days
e: Section 64VB requires that premium be received by the insurer, or guaranteed to be paid, before the insurer assumes the risk.
